highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159 previews programmable GPU meshes and an experimental image-comparison package on Skia m159.
highlights_body: The line also improves runtime-effect uniform initialization, Windows image-decoder recovery, Apple device frameworks and filtered texture sampling. WebAssembly requires .NET 9 or later, and Linux x86 native assets are removed; non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support remains unchanged.

breaking.title: Move WebAssembly applications to .NET 9 or later
breaking.body: SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp no longer provide .NET 8 WebAssembly native assets, and packaged targets reject unsupported WASM frameworks. Retarget WASM applications to .NET 9 or later and use the runtime-matched archives rather than substituting newer archives into .NET 8. Non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support is unchanged.

breaking.title: Replace Linux x86 deployments
breaking.body: Linux x86 native builds and NuGet package entries are removed. Applications relying on those assets must move to a supported Linux architecture, such as x64, before adopting this line's updated packages.

bullets.detail: Updates the native renderer with WebAssembly SIMD CPU rasterization, Windows font-loading improvements and image/rendering correctness fixes, then incorporates subsequent m159 upstream fixes. The milestone transition itself leaves C API exports and public managed signatures unchanged.

SKMesh specifications compile SkSL vertex and fragment programs for indexed or non-indexed drawing through SKCanvas.DrawMesh, with builders, uniforms, children and CPU or Ganesh GPU buffers. Built meshes retain the native references they need after input wrappers are disposed. Drawing requires a GPU-backed surface; raster drawing is a no-op.

The separate SkiaSharp.Testing package adds SKImageComparison for images, bitmaps and pixmaps, with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets, MAE/RMS/PSNR metrics and five difference-image styles. The assembly is experimental under SKIA4001. Results retain no native handles; generated difference images are independent caller-owned SKImage instances.

New SKRuntimeEffectUniforms buffers start zeroed rather than containing leftover memory. Reset clears the existing buffer in place without allocating a replacement, including uniforms used by mesh builders.

Windows x64 clang builds avoid crashes when libjpeg or libpng recovers from decoding errors, including lazy non-JPEG PDF images and malformed JPEGs passed to SKCodec.Create. CFG remains enabled; arm64, x86 and MSVC builds are unchanged.
MAUI SKGLView uses a typed Window binding to eliminate the warning caused by a runtime string-path binding in trimmed applications. The proxy-window binding behavior is unchanged.

bullets.lead: Texture sampling and CPU blur selection
bullets.detail: Ganesh uses an inward inset for filtered texture-subset edges, avoiding undefined exterior texels; this does not change CPU or Graphite sampling. Tizen now applies its intended CPU blur setting to Skia itself, selecting the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent path instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Texture-edge and Tizen blur pixels may differ.

Mask-filtered glyphs use reloaded paths, formats and full plane strides, clearing incompatible masks safely. Image-filter cache equality matches hashing. Imagination Vulkan descriptor pools are deliberately abandoned after affected out-of-memory errors rather than destroyed, trading cleanup for driver safety.

SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp iOS/tvOS device frameworks contain only arm64 device binaries and matching metadata, avoiding simulator slices that could cause App Store validation failure ITMS-90087. Simulator frameworks and symbols retain their x86_64 and arm64 slices.

contributor_summaries.taublast: Zero-initialized runtime-effect uniforms, allocation-free Reset and disposal of test data snapshots.
contributor_summaries.kdpkke: Correct iOS/tvOS device frameworks and preserved simulator outputs.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored Uno Gallery projects to the Windows sample solution.
contributor_summaries.SimonCropp: Windows x64 libjpeg/libpng error-recovery crash workaround.

preview_summaries.v4.159.0-rc.1.26567.13: Release Candidate 1 adds programmable GPU mesh drawing and corrects SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp Apple device frameworks. It also includes glyph-rendering, image-filter cache and Imagination Vulkan allocation fixes.
preview_summaries.v4.159.0-preview.1.26563.22: Preview 1 introduces Skia m159 with WebAssembly SIMD rasterization and Windows font-loading improvements. WebAssembly now requires .NET 9 or later; non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support is unchanged.

harfbuzz_summary: HarfBuzzSharp package revision 15.0.0.100 retains native HarfBuzz 15.0.0. The collected changes remove .NET 8 WebAssembly and Linux x86 native assets and correct iOS/tvOS device frameworks while preserving simulator slices.

v4.159.0-preview.1.26563.22.headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 Preview 1 introduces Skia m159 with WebAssembly SIMD rasterization and Windows font-loading improvements.
v4.159.0-preview.1.26563.22.body: WebAssembly consumers now require .NET 9 or later; non-WebAssembly .NET 8 support is unchanged. HarfBuzzSharp package revision 15.0.0.100 retains native HarfBuzz 15.0.0.

v4.159.0-rc.1.26567.13.headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 Release Candidate 1 adds programmable GPU mesh drawing.
v4.159.0-rc.1.26567.13.body: Custom SkSL mesh programs support indexed and non-indexed geometry on GPU-backed surfaces; raster drawing is a no-op. This candidate also corrects SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp iOS/tvOS device frameworks and incorporates glyph-rendering, image-filter cache, and Imagination Vulkan allocation fixes.
